_readme: Copy to check-files.json and adapt to the application routes. No secret: same identities as check-http.json (token_cmd / token_env).

Relative paths (manifest, command of token_cmd): resolved from the folder of THIS file, not from the current directory. Here storage-manifest.json and scripts/forge-token.mjs are next to check-files.json.
manifest: the one from migrate-storage.py; each PASS object is re-read through the application and its SHA-256 compared with the source one.
read.path and upload.path: templates {bucket} and {name} (encoded in the URL); upload.fields: raw {name}, {id:alice}, {random}.
read.identities: who re-reads each migrated file, as a list or per bucket ({"avatars": ["anon"], "*": []}); the owner is always added. Only identities that the SOURCE policies allow.
upload.format: 'multipart' (file_field + fields) or 'raw' (body = the file, type in Content-Type, e.g. PUT /api/files/{name}).

refused: cases taken from the source policies (someone else's file, write on behalf of someone else). 'upload': true for a write. status: list of accepted codes. On a migrated object, the owner re-reads it afterwards: intact bytes required.

A 409 on 'bob overwrites alice's avatar' proves the (bucket_id, name) uniqueness, NOT the UPDATE policy. replacement: the route that replaces an existing file (upsert); others must be refused (bytes intact), the owner accepted (new bytes re-read). Without such a route: test the UPDATE policy in SQL (reference/storage.md §8).
purge: deletion route; the objects uploaded by the check (including a refused or accepted HTML) are deleted at the end. Without it, their list is printed at the end, to purge by hand.
CELLAR_ADDON_HOST in the environment (not a secret) enables the direct anonymous access check on the bucket (403 expected).

refused.name: bob reads a private document of alice -> 403/404
